title: Reverse Number
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, return the number with its digits reversed.
mnemonic: Take last digit, build new number
think: What is the task asking? Reverse the order of digits in the number.
What is the key operation? Extract the last digit repeatedly.
What wording signals stand out? Reverse number, digits.
Which pattern fits? Linear Scan over digits.
What is the brute force idea? Convert to string, reverse, parse back.
What is the better/optimal idea? Use modulo and division mathematically.
What are the edge cases? 0, trailing zeros like 1200.
What is the complexity? O(d) time and O(1) space where d is number of digits.
How would I explain it in an interview? I repeatedly take the last digit with % 10 and append it to the result.
interview: I would reverse the number mathematically by repeatedly taking the last digit and appending it to the result.
ru: На каждом шаге берём последнюю цифру числа и добавляем её в новое число справа.

critical: Forget to update n inside the loop
important: Lose the place value when appending digits
nice: Do not mention trailing zeros behavior

gaps: Important: understand modulo and integer division
Nice to have: compare math solution vs string solution
constraints: Assume input is non-negative and result fits in int.
whyThisPattern: This is a straightforward digit-processing scan with repeated modulo/division operations.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Two Pointers, because we are not traversing a sequence from both ends.
Not Dictionary, because there is no counting.
